title: Investigate customer JSON eval regressions after sampling seed reset and stop-sequence mismatch
creator: Lina Kapoor
description: A high-severity customer (redacted) reported reproducible eval regressions: their JSON-structured outputs are being truncated or contain extra tokens after we rolled runtime-1.22 with a sampling defaults change and the new retry path. The regression surfaced in both Hosted and Dedicated where requests flow through the new sampling proxy that performs lightweight retry/merge logic. Symptoms include missing final JSON keys, corrupted closing braces, and mismatched stop-sequence behavior compared to pre-1.22. Customer eval suites that previously passed with stable stop-token termination are now flaky or failing deterministically in some workloads.
reproduction_steps: 1) Use customer's eval prompt (redacted) targeting structured JSON output with explicit stop sequences ['\n\n', '### END'].
2) Call Redwood hosted endpoint runtime-1.22 with sampling defaults (top_p=0.95, temp=0.8) and enable automatic retry (default).
3) Observe output: missing final JSON field 'diagnosis' in 12% of runs, and sometimes an extra '\ufffd' byte near end; reproduction rate higher on long-context prompts.
4) Repeat on Dedicated pool with same model and routing policy -> similar failure pattern when routing through sampling proxy node.
5) Run with sampling disabled (deterministic decode) or pin to runtime-1.21 -> outputs match baseline and JSON is intact.
investigation_findings: - Initial hypothesis: stop-sequence matching regression due to change in stop token normalization.

- Reproduced locally: when a retry occurs, the sampling RNG seed was being reset incorrectly; subsequent token probabilities diverge causing stop token not to be emitted at the same point as the baseline.

- Found a secondary issue: stop-sequence matching performed on byte-level post-processing in the routing layer rather than on token boundaries, so in some multi-byte UTF-8 sequences the stop check missed a match.
- Correlation: failures spike when retry merge runs (fast retry) and for prompts with multi-byte characters at boundaries (e.g., emojis, non-latin scripts).
- Logs: sampling proxy logs show retry seed=0x0 being reused in ~3% of cases due to uninitialized RNG state in the retry path (see PR and logs).
- Existing unit tests didn't cover retry seed continuity or token-aware stop matching; integration tests relied on exact string match causing false confidence.
mitigation_actions: 1) Hotfix: set deterministic continuation of RNG seed across retry path in sampling proxy and add guard to prevent uninitialized seed (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4123).
2) Patch: change routing-layer stop-sequence remover to operate on tokenized output (token ids and boundaries) instead of raw bytes for runtime-1.22 patch release.

3) Immediate customer-facing mitigation: one-off config to disable automatic retry for affected customers and roll back sampling defaults to runtime-1.21 behavior while patch lands (communicated to customer on 2026-03-11).
4) Add emergency smoke test case to CI that runs customer's eval set end-to-end on a gated pre-release job.
rollout_plan: - Stage 1 (canary): merge hotfix to canary runtime pool (1 host) and run customer's eval suite 500 iterations overnight.
- Stage 2 (limited): deploy token-aware stop matching to 10% of routing nodes; monitor JSON truncation rate and error budgets.
- Stage 3 (general): full rollout to Hosted and Dedicated after 48h of canary metrics stability and one successful customer validation run.
- Fallback: if instability returns, open immediate rollback to runtime-1.21 default sampling profile for affected customers.
test_plan: - Unit tests: add deterministic RNG continuity tests for retry path and token-aware stop-sequence matcher tests.
- Integration: reproduce customer's eval suite on a dedicated staging pool with varied charsets (emojis, CJK) and ensure zero truncations across 1k runs.
- Regression: add a nightly job that runs a representative set of structured-output evals to detect similar regressions early.
- Post-release: run customer-provided evals for 7 days and publish aggregated pass/fail metrics to customer dashboard.
acceptance_criteria: - Hotfix merged and canary run shows <0.1% JSON truncation vs baseline for customer's suite.
- Token-aware stop matching implemented and covered by unit tests.
- CI integration test prevents regressions by failing PRs that introduce retry seed discontinuity or byte-level stop checks.
- Customer confirms restored parity for their evals and signs off on closure.
